title: im literally in highschool with zero coding experience and just made a 1940s FPS game using AI (Barnaby early alpha demo)
author: DegTrader
selftext:
hey guys, im still in high school and literally have zero coding background, but i always wanted to try making a game. i thought you needed a CS degree to even touch physics, but i spent the last few weeks using AI to help me build a prototype called *Barnaby*.

it’s a goofy 1940s slapstick FPS where you play as a 300lb mouse swinging between skyscrapers with sticky cheese strings  the swinging physics were a total nightmare to fix through prompting, and the AI kept breaking my scripts once the file got too big, but seeing it actually work made me really want to learn real programming now.

its super rough and full of bugs, but i put a free early alpha build on itch if anyone wants to check it out or drop some feedback:[https://vanzim2.itch.io/barnaby](https://vanzim2.itch.io/barnaby)

any tips from real devs on how to stop LLMs from overwriting good code when fixing bugs? still super new to all this so any advice helps!

comments.author: bobmefred
comments.body: unit tests will help claude not break stuff thats working

comments.author: SushiMasterPro
comments.body: Good luck! Its really cool you started that young! Enjoy your journey and try to improve every day. You are already ahead most of your schoolmates dont spend time learning and improving!

comments.author: drahgon
comments.body: The thing about ai is everyone is learning right now especially with gaming. I’m a programmer and we are making it up as we go. Vibecoding has never been done before. Just tell it the bugs and through trial and error try to get it to make a system that can get you consistent results. Definitely have it test features that it adds for quality.

comments.author: Good-Acanthaceae-136
comments.body:
So how is this going to move away from a prototype if you have zero programming knowledge?

Anyone that tries making a game with no knowledge of anything isn't going to get far and will end up with slop. Spend your time at least learning some basics. Plus this art style is already really overdone at this point.

comments.author: Raqnarock
comments.body: Can't give you any technical feedback outside of learning to prompt for the things that you want by being specific. I like the idea of what you have so far, its very goofy but memorable.

comments.author: cheyumaama
comments.body: People still go to high school? Thought that fad died out with us

comments.author: HugoDzz
comments.body: that looks really cool! I'd recommend to add a bit of RGB shift (ask LLM to do it), it will make the retro look a bit more realistic!

comments.author: Advice2Anyone
comments.body: I mean all I know is you gotta be very deliberate with your word usage there is a difference between hey move that tree closer and move that tree 20 pts closer to the player area.
